sentences.text: 2  JUDGMENT Heard learned counsel Sri. Sharanappa S. Koliwad, Gururaj R.Turumari, Siddappa S. Sajjan for Sri.B.V.Somapaur and Sri.Nagaraj C. Kollori.

2. Though, matter is listed for admission, with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties,
matter is taken up for final disposal.
3. Insurance company is in appeal challenging the award passed in MVC No.456/2013 dated 07.10.2016 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT., Ramdurg, District Saundatti.

4. Facts in brief which are utmost necessary for disposal of the appear are as under:
4.1 In respect of road traffic accident occurred on 07.04.2011 involving tum-tum (auto-rickshaw) bearing No.KA-24/5618 and truck bearing No.KA-25/7833, injured claimant who is first respondent in the appeal laid a claim.
Another injured also laid a claim and said claim petition NC: 2024:KHC-D:806 was registered as MVC No.1052/2013 and first respondent claim petition was registered as MVC No.456/2013.
Both the cases were clubbed and disposed of by a common judgment dated 07.10.2016 granting compensation in a sum of Rs.4,32,000/- in respect of accidental claim in MVC No.456/2013 after contest.
4.2. Being aggrieved with the quantum of compensation and fastening the entire liability on the insurance company, appellant has preferred the present appeal.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, Sri.S.S.Koliwad vehemently contended that injured is a minor and therefore following the principal of law enunciated in Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, the National Insurance Company Limited and another,
reported in AIR 2014 SC 736, the quantum of compensation awarded in a sum of Rs.4,32,000/- is on higher side and sought for reduction of quantum of compensation.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, the National Insurance Company Limited and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also contended that in respect of the claim petition in MVC No.1052/2013, insurance company has filed appeal wherein this court has fastened the liability at 50%.

He also contended that in respect of MVC No.640/2012 which is another claim in respect of same question, involving same vehicles in MFA No.23504/2013, this court has apportioned the liability to the extent of 50% on the insurance company of the truck and 50% on the three wheeler pick up van which was not properly insured and 50% liability is fastened on the owner of the pick up vehicle on the ground that the injured was unauthorized passenger.
7. Sri. S.S.Koliwad sought for passing similar order in the present case.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel Sri.G.R.Turumuri supported the impugned judgment.
9. So also, the other respondents supported the impugned judgment.
Perused the material available on record meticulously.
11. On such perusal, admittedly, minor claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident involving the aforesaid vehicle is not in dispute.

12. Following the dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Master Mallikarjuna supra, claimant would be entitled for a compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as against sum of Rs.3,00,000/-
ordered by the tribunal and for attendant charges, food and nourishment and transportation charges
, claimant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.32,000/-, 25,000/- and Rs.15,000/- as ordered by the tribunal.

13. Further, this court in MFA No.23504/2013 has already recorded a categorical finding that the injured being unauthorized passenger, 50% of the liability is to be fastened on the owner of tum-tum(auto-rickshaw) and NC: 2024:KHC-D:806 balance 50% has to be fastened on the insurance company of the truck.
14. Owner of the tum-tum(auto-rickshaw) has not challenged the said order.

15. Therefore, need has arisen to pass similar order in the present appeal by fastening the 50%
liability on the owner of the tum-tum(auto-rickshaw) bearing No.KA- 24/5618.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.

ii) As against sum of Rs.4,32,000/- awarded by the tribunal, claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,72,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire amount.

iii) Out of adjudged compensation, 50% shall be payable by the appellant and balance 50% NC: 2024:KHC-D:806 of the compensation is to be paid the owner of the tum-tum (auto-rickshaw) bearing No.KA- 24/5618.
iv) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to the tribunal and excess amount if any is ordered to be returned to the appellant-insurance company under due identification.
